text:
maria: quick async standup — morning pulse from me

maria: yesterday: rolled kv-cache eviction tuning to canary (region-us-west), added a short TTL for preds cache, ran load test at p95 ~ stable but p99 bumped ~8% for text-gen routes.

maria: blocker: still seeing occasional synthetic check failures on the prefix-cache job around 03:12 UTC — unsure if it's eviction timing or a race with batching. logs look like `KVCache: miss; inflight=true` a few times.

maria: today: revert option prepared if p99 stays high; want a quick config review on the TTL change and a prod runbook note for oncall fallback. also pinging for cr on PR #4321 (kv-evict: short-ttl, tests added).

kevin: saw the p99 too. thanks for the canary. can you paste the exact metric query? i'll check HPA and GPU saturation too.

maria: metric is `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/text-gen"}[5m])) by (le))` filtered by instance and region-us-west-canary.

priya: re: synthetic flaps — i saw similar around 03:10 in eu-west, but it recovered. my hunch is batching interaction at small batch sizes when a node gets hot. added a 1s jitter in the batcher in a branch earlier (not rolled).

lee: @maria @priya can we correlate kernel selection logs? if the runtime switches a quantized kernel, latency can jump for a few tokens while caches warm. i can run a debug job that dumps kernel choice and kv-stats for a sample window.

maria: ok that would be great. if you can run it against the canary pool that'd be ideal. i'll attach request ids when i see failures.

kevin: on oncall notes — suggested temporary mute for alert `high-req-latency-noise` for the canary group, but keep page for >=5min sustained. otherwise we're getting noise. thoughts? :thinking_face: 

dana: +1 to throttle notifications for canary. but include an automatic unmute in 30m so we don't blind ourselves if it keeps rising. also add a link to rollback runbook in the alert message.

maria: agreed. i'll update the alert policy: threshold same, but change notification to #eng-sre for immediate chatter and page only after 5m sustained. add rollback link (docs/runbooks/kv-evict-rollback).

priya: quick CR note: PR #4321 has a unit test that simulates concurrent inflight fetches. i added a comment about potential flakiness and a small sleep that can be flaky on CI — i'd prefer a deterministic barrier.

maria: noted — i'll replace sleep with a signal channel.

deploy-bot: deploy started: kv-evict-ttl-canary -> us-west (id: dpl-20260317-11)

maria: thanks deploy-bot. i'll watch the dashboard and paste any failing request ids here.

lee: also a follow-up: can we add a one-off synthetic that hits a long-prefix case to exercise prefix cache edge? if we can reproduce locally it's faster.

kevin: i'll schedule the synthetic and post results in this thread. aiming for a run in 15m.

maria: last ask: oncall handover — @dana you'll take the next 4-hour window, check the canary dashboard at top of hour and mute/unmute per the policy. i'll leave a short checklist in the handoff doc.

dana: got it. i'll monitor and escalate if page fires.

kevin: quick FYI — i opened a ticket to look at HPA and minor GC tuning on the canary nodes: TKT-5782. linking here for context.

maria: perfect. thanks everyone. will post updates if I see more p99 drift or synthetic failures. :thumbsup:
